name: MathCircles.org (National Association of Math Circles)
what_it_is: The resource site of the National Association of Math Circles: 103 published
activities, each a session a facilitator can run with a group. Every activity carries
a taxonomy (audience, topic, materials) and most attach one or more PDFs.
It is a facilitator resource site, not a problem bank. Read what_to_expect below.

audience_spread.comment: The 6th-12th bands map onto 4e to Terminale almost exactly, which is why this source was chosen.

what_to_expect: Most files are facilitator lesson plans, not problem sets. The Criss-Cross handout is
typical: two pages of 'Have students...', 'Ask them...', then nine problems at the end.
A file can look rich and carry one classic: Fay-ZenkTrioofFriendlyProblems.pdf is 29
pages of teaching steps whose entire mathematical content is the handshake count, and
it was excluded for that reason.
The Tom Davis handouts (catalan, diophantine, pickTomDavis, bignumbers) are expository
articles with problems embedded in prose, the same shape as the UCLA material.
Almost nothing carries a worked solution, so the importer solves and verifies everything.
Expect a low keep rate. Read a file, take the two or three problems that stand on their
own, record the rest with reasons.
overlap_warning: This site leans on famous classics, and the collection already holds many of them from
Moscow, Lyon and UCLA. Checked before the run: the lockers problem is already 0303,
knights-and-liars appear in 8 files, Euler-characteristic material in 10, Koenigsberg
is 0234, the handshake count is already in.
Genuine gaps this source can fill: Pick's theorem (0 in the collection), magic squares
(0), tilings and Escher (0), Catalan numbers (1), rational tangles (0), Voronoi (0).
ALWAYS search the database by statement before writing, never by source filename.
how_it_was_enumerated: WordPress REST API: /wp-json/wp/v2/activity (103 records, taxonomy ids) and
built with Elementor, so content is empty over the API and the file links had to be
scraped from each activity's HTML. Taxonomy names come from /wp-json/wp/v2/audience,

external_only_activities.what: Activities with no file of their own; they link to mathcommunities.org (14), Google Drive (11), YouTube (17), mathpickle.com (6), jrmf.org (5) and others. Out of scope by decision: this import covers files hosted on mathcircles.org only.

not_imported.comment: The seven files above have no text layer at all. They are real activities, not junk, and a later pass can recover them by rendering pages at 300 dpi and reading them by eye. See sources/namc/excluded.json for the full exclusion list with reasons.
